memo.verdict: Park. Neutral direction, medium conviction (a Triaging read from four uncited research digests written before the results and one fully cited earnings review). The record's own words: Alfen is a self-help recovery laid over a policy-driven Dutch grid demand cycle, and at €11.58 (2026-09-18) it is not a compelling case; the change inside the company is broad and real but has reached the balance sheet and one operating metric, not the profit line, while the shares already trade at 25.30 times twenty-four-month-forward consensus earnings, so the earnings recovery is largely spent paying for the multiple to normalise. The framework's park rule applies twice, on management (no mediocre management, D) and on business quality (the Business Element, D), and the record does not argue against it; predictability (transmission, D) is a third application. Not bearish, because the balance sheet (net cash €6.2m at June 2026), the grid franchise and the sell-side capitulation bound the downside over the three-month horizon of the price patterns. The case re-opens below about €10.50, where the 'Modal return' clears 20% a year at both horizons on our path (that level is also the sell-side's median target), or at any price on evidence of a first-quarter 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin of 8% together with third-quarter 2026 storage order intake above €50m. What to watch: the 'Case/SP Key Drivers and Risks' Element.
case: - The change inside the company is broad, real and in the accounts. New chief executive, chair and interim finance director; three business units from 1 May 2026; headcount cut about 15% to 909; inventory to €72.3m; the DC charger discontinued; the revolving facility halved to €50m; net debt €20.7m turned into net cash €6.2m. Four of twelve internal forces are strong (chief-executive change; strategy and structure; standards improvement; perimeter reduction), passing the screen's rule of at least three. The one internal signal pointing the other way is guidance, which has only moved down.

- The external force that matters is a structural, dated grid tailwind that the company converts only as fast as its customers can build. Over 14,000 parties wait for Dutch connections; the three operators controlling about 94% of Dutch secondary substations have record capital plans for 2026 to 2028; a fast-track permitting regime for projects of 21kV and above starts 7 October 2026. Alfen holds about 70% of Dutch secondary substations. Management says the fast-track brings no volume in FY2026 because the constraint is technicians and permits; two operators downscaled 2025 orders for lack of labour. Charging and storage face headwinds, not tailwinds.

- Along the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain the change has reached resources, choices, actions, the balance sheet and substation volumes, and not gross margin (26.1% from 30.0%), earnings per share (-€0.09 in FY26 on our path) or the sell-side's FY26 estimates (-€0.149 mean, cut 184% in three months).
counter_case: - At its strongest: Alfen is a net-cash utility-supply franchise at the start of a decade-long, policy-mandated grid reinforcement cycle, priced at about half its revenue and about 8 times next year's consensus EBITDA, with a sell-side at zero buys of eight, the highest short position on Euronext Amsterdam (7.6% of share capital), a fixed-cost base built for twice today's revenue, a management that has delivered its first-year promises (the three-unit structure on 1 May 2026; the cash), and a 5 GWh sodium-ion partnership with CATL that puts it first in Europe on the cheapest storage chemistry. The charging and storage noise is what a buyer is paid to tolerate. FY27 EBITDA of €33m (Jefferies, 20 August 2026) and a return to the five-year median multiple give a share price near €18 within two years; a takeover (no protection), a buyback (a 10% authorisation to October 2027) or a sodium-ion reference project brings it forward.

- Against 'Foundations' D: the foundations that matter are the grid ones and they are strong: a 70% share held since relationships formed in 1937; physical barriers (a substation weighs over 1,000 times an EV charger), regulatory barriers (country grid codes, SF6-free certification) and early specification into standards; frameworks covering 70% of Smart Grid revenue; three customers with 94% of the market and record budgets; pricing discipline. On that reading a B on 'Foundations' follows.
triggers: - Re-open the case below about €10.50, or at any price on a first-quarter 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin of 8% with third-quarter 2026 storage intake above €50m.

- Invalidate levels on the four 'Case/SP Key Drivers': quarterly substation deliveries below 800 (grid conversion); H2 2026 adjusted EBITDA below €4m or a first-quarter 2027 margin below 5% (the cost base after the overlap); fourth-quarter 2026 charging revenue below €24m (charging stabilisation, and the home-charging price war as its inverse); third-quarter 2026 storage intake below €30m (storage order intake, and cell-maker disintermediation).
- Alarm level: a first-quarter 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin below 8% keeps the case parked.

- The 'Case/SP Key Risks': the multiple on trough earnings (a share-price risk; probable that it compresses towards 18x; the skew to 12.23x, -52%, on unchanged earnings); mis-execution recurring in the finance seat (a case risk; watch a permanent finance-director appointment and whether FY26 guidance holds); the home-charging price war (both tests; probable, worsening); storage disintermediation by cell makers (a case risk; plausible, moving against Alfen; sodium-ion hedges cost, not channel).

- The depreciation line: 13.6 EURm reported in FY25 against 22 to 23 EURm implied by consensus medians; at 22 EURm the eighteen-month return falls to 3.8% a year; unverifiable from the disclosure; also the one named line under 'Compounder', a watch item and not a pass.

- Near steps: the fast-track regime from 7 October 2026; the third-quarter 2026 trading update (storage intake, substation count); the new home charger; the FY26 results on 17 February 2027 with any FY27 guidance; a permanent finance-director appointment. Mid steps: the first-quarter 2027 margin; first sodium-ion project orders; Southern European and German grid wins; the H1 2027 results as the first clean half. Far steps: sodium-ion deployments from H2 2027; the European grid capital-expenditure cycle; possible use of the buyback authorisation.
